title: How the Endpoint Order Deposit Is Built from the ClearPath Relationship
content:
The deposit on the approval of a Hardware Procurement Standard Endpoint Order or Staged Endpoint Order quote is built by the client's ClearPath Managed IT Services relationship:

1. A client with no active ClearPath agreement pays a deposit equal to the distributor cost of the units, the distributor unit cost times the quantity, whatever the percentage.
2. A client whose active ClearPath agreement went live fewer than **36** whole months before the approval date pays the order's service charges, the quote total less the quantity times the unit price, in full, plus the deposit percentage of the quantity times the unit price.
3. Every other client pays the deposit percentage of the quote total.

Whole months are counted from the go-live date, a month completing only once the day of the month reaches the go-live date's day number. The go-live date is the one on the client's ClearPath agreement whose status is active.

## The three builds, worked (hypothetical quote; percentage taken as 20 for the illustration)

Hypothetical quote: 5 units, distributor unit cost 1000.00, unit price 1150.00, quote total 6225.00 (the units at 5750.00 plus 475.00 of service charges).

| Client | Build | Deposit |
|---|---|---|
| no active ClearPath agreement | distributor cost of the units | 5 times 1000.00, that is 5000.00 |
| active agreement live 35 whole months | service charges in full plus 20 percent of the units | 475.00 plus 1150.00, that is 1625.00 |
| active agreement live 36 whole months | 20 percent of the quote total | 1245.00 |

**Boundary of the tenure band.** For an agreement that went live on the 10th of a month, on the 9th of the month 36 months later only 35 whole months have completed; on the 10th the 36th month completes and the client moves to the third build.
